title: Assess interval overlap enrichment with Fisher's exact test
source_kind: documented CLI operation and worked statistical example

sources.locator: Purpose, worked example, Evaluation, Usage and option summary

scientific_use: Estimate whether two genomic interval sets overlap more than expected given their interval coverage and genome size, producing counts, a contingency table and Fisher exact-test tail p-values.
tool_role_basis: The source presents a command that analyzes two BED sets and a genome-size file using bedtools fisher; its inferential algorithm is supplied by the package.
inputs: Two sorted BED/GFF/VCF interval collections and chromosome-size genome file.
Example uses three intervals and two intervals on a 500-base toy chromosome; this is documentation data, not a biological study.
outputs: Overlap/unique interval counts, estimated possible interval count, contingency table, left/right/two-tail p-values and ratio.
dependencies: bedtools fisher CLI
Inputs sorted by chromosome and start coordinate per manual; genome size and interval-length assumptions influence estimate.
evidence: Fisher manual states scientific question and gives complete toy invocation/output
Evaluation section compares p-values with shuffling over canonical chr1 genes and random intervals, and cautions that low p-values merit simulation validation
limitations: Possible interval count uses a heuristic based on mean interval sizes and genome size; manual reports inflation in the described evaluation.
No input study dataset is bundled with this operation; authors must decide whether inferential assumptions suit the task.

title: Characterize spatial proximity between genomic interval sets
source_kind: documented CLI operation with packaged-data examples

sources.locator: Metric definition, default behavior and examples using packaged exon/AluY and exon/GERP files

scientific_use: Describe how close intervals in set A are to the two closest intervals in B, as a distribution over relative distances 0 to 0.5. A uniform distribution is the documented null expectation; concentration at small distances suggests spatial proximity even when intervals rarely overlap. Manual examples compare RefSeq exons with AluY repeats and GERP conservation intervals.
tool_role_basis: The manual applies bedtools reldist to existing packaged BED assets and interprets the returned distance distribution.
inputs: Two interval sets; documented examples use data/refseq.chr1.exons.bed.gz against data/aluY.chr1.bed.gz or data/gerp.chr1.bed.gz.
outputs: Binned relative-distance distribution (or per-A intervals with detail option), with counts/fractions.
dependencies: bedtools reldist CLI
BED-compatible interval files; manual describes comparison to a uniform distribution as null expectation.
